title: Is rainfall changing in the Klang Valley?
subtitle: Average daily rainfall, Malaysia, 1990-2025

variable.name: Precipitation (bias-corrected)
variable.definition: Average rainfall per day, averaged over each month. A reanalysis product that blends a weather model with satellite and gauge rainfall data.
variable.caveat: Rainfall is highly variable from year to year (e.g. El Nino/La Nina), so short records can mislead. Reanalysis rainfall is an estimate, not a gauge measurement.
variable.source: NASA MERRA-2 reanalysis, accessed via NASA POWER

raw.method: Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope on raw monthly values (ignores seasons & autocorrelation)
raw.plain: Annual average rainfall rose by about 0.515 mm/day per decade (95% CI 0.25 to 0.781), p = 0.000: statistically significant.

deseasonalized.method: Hamed-Rao modified Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope on monthly anomalies
deseasonalized.plain: Annual average rainfall rose by about 0.486 mm/day per decade (95% CI 0.273 to 0.695), p = 0.000: statistically significant.

seasonal_mk.method: Seasonal Mann-Kendall (each calendar month tested separately, then pooled) + Sen's slope
seasonal_mk.plain: Annual average rainfall rose by about 0.454 mm/day per decade (95% CI 0.225 to 0.692), p = 0.000: statistically significant.

season_only.method: Mann-Kendall + Sen's slope on yearly Whole year means
season_only.plain: Annual average rainfall rose by about 0.464 mm/day per decade (95% CI 0.234 to 0.705), p = 0.000: statistically significant.

metrics.verdict_text: Whether the trend looks real depends on which years you pick: its size, direction or significance changes between periods. Treat any single-period result with caution, and check which years or events drive it.

notes: Regional value = average of 4 MERRA-2 grid cells inside the region (about 0.5 x 0.6 degrees each).
Reanalysis data blend a weather model with satellite and ground observations; trends can be affected by changes in the observing system.
Heatmap windows overlap heavily, so it is a descriptive sensitivity view, not many independent tests.
'Not significant' does not mean 'no trend' - a longer record may be needed.

Annual means rise partly because 2021-2025 were very wet years in this reanalysis; check the heatmap to see how much the conclusion depends on the end year. Changes in the observations assimilated by reanalyses can also create artificial steps.
